m_obs,i = 1 if coordinate i was directly observed;  m_obs,i = 0 if it was missing, invalid, or imputed.

Figure 12.1 - Canonical self-healing transport pipeline. Repair restores computational continuity while provenance remains explicit.
12.2 Validity semantics: zero is a valid latent value
The audited SnowPulse validation path used std::isnormal on latent coordinates. That predicate rejects zero and subnormal values in addition to NaN and infinity. Unless the model intentionally forbids exact zero, this creates a semantic bug: the all-zero state is marked invalid even though zero is a finite value inside the nominal latent interval.
Recommended predicate:  valid(z_i) := isfinite(z_i) AND (-1 <= z_i <= 1).
If subnormals are intentionally flushed for hardware reasons, that should be an explicit quantization policy rather than an accidental consequence of the validity predicate.

Figure 12.2 - The observation mask remains separate from the repaired numerical state.
12.3 Howard repair: projection scale and residual must remain typed
For observed coordinates O and a frozen template k, the least-squares scale is computed only on observed support:
lambda_L2 = [sum_{i in O} z_i k_i] / [sum_{i in O} k_i^2].
Missing coordinates may then be repaired by z_i := lambda_L2 k_i, but the repaired positions remain marked unobserved. Residual statistics must also state which support set they use.
rho_L1 = (1/|O|) sum_{i in O} |z_i - lambda_L2 k_i|.
Because lambda_L2 minimizes squared error while rho_L1 measures absolute error, the two are valid together but solve different optimization problems. A robustness diagnostic is obtained by also computing the L1-optimal scale.
lambda_L1 = weightedMedian( z_i / k_i ; weights |k_i| ), for k_i != 0.
R_lambda = |lambda_L2 - lambda_L1|.
12.4 Projection into the admissible ball
Let P denote the declared projection into the admissible latent ball. A common radial form is
P(z) = z, if ||z||_2 <= 1-eps;    P(z) = [(1-eps)/||z||_2] z, otherwise.
The important point is not the choice of radial projection itself, but when metadata are measured. The previously audited SnowPulse path computed lambda, rho, phi, and admission metadata before the final projection and then transmitted the projected state. When projection changes z, the metadata can describe a different state from the bytes actually sent.

Figure 12.3 - Transport congruence requires recomputation of metadata after any state-changing projection.
12.5 Coverage loss and bounded quantization error
Let phi in [0,1] represent a declared missing-information or missing-kernel-energy fraction. If it is transported as an 8-bit floor quantization
q_phi = floor(255 phi),      phi_q = q_phi / 255,
then
0 <= phi - phi_q < 1/255 = 0.00392156862745... .
Thus floor quantization systematically understates phi. Any gate that becomes looser as phi decreases can therefore admit a state that the unquantized value would refuse when the true state lies sufficiently close to the boundary.
For a threshold theta(phi) = theta0 (1 - c phi), the maximum threshold loosening caused by flooring is
0 <= theta(phi_q) - theta(phi) < theta0 c / 255.
For c = 1/2, the gap is less than theta0/510. A safe implementation either rounds conservatively in the refusal direction, transports sufficient precision, or carries an explicit quantization margin in the gate.
12.6 SA-ZDP frame semantics and FP16 boundaries
The packed SA-ZDP frame used in the current corpus occupies eight declared bytes: float32 lambda_star, uint16 rho_fp16, uint8 phi_quant, and uint8 valid_mask. Its compactness is useful, but the fields must not be assigned semantics they cannot carry.

The previously supplied custom FP16 conversion also flushes sufficiently small values to signed zero and maps exponent overflow to infinity. That behavior is an implementation policy, not lossless transport.

That padding is not a portable transport resource: compilers and ABIs are free to lay out objects differently within the language rules.
If a 320-byte fixed record is desirable, the 48 bytes should be declared as actual schema fields rather than inferred from padding. The audited pipeline used a 128-dimensional latent coverage quantity to tighten a 5-dimensional kinetic/tangent gate. That coupling is not automatically justified because the two quantities live in different state spaces. Introduce an explicit bridge

12.10 Shared-memory ring semantics and producer ownership
A ring-buffer push path that obtains the head with load(), writes a slot, and later advances the head with store() can be correct for a deliberately single-producer design. It is not a general multi-producer reservation algorithm: two producers can read the same head and target the same slot before either store becomes visible.

Figure 12.5 - Single-producer ring semantics do not automatically generalize to multiple producers.
For MPMC operation, use an algorithm with explicit slot ownership, such as compare-and-swap reservation, fetch-add with sequence discipline, or per-slot generation counters. Memory-ordering and object-lifetime rules must also be documented. If the ring spans processes, the implementation must additionally guarantee that the chosen atomic representation is supported for shared interprocess memory on the target platform.

13.1 Bridge definition and semantic boundary
Let z_t in R^128 denote the provenance-aware latent state after validation, repair, and final transmitted-state projection. Let y_t in R^5 denote the kinetic state used for trajectory and tangent analysis. A bridge is an explicitly declared map
B : R^128 -> R^5,     y_hat_t = B(z_t).
The bridge is a model. It is not an identity between latent and kinetic spaces, and it does not make a latent diagnostic automatically valid as a kinetic diagnostic. Every transported quantity requires its own compatibility test.

Figure 13.1 - A 128-D to 5-D bridge is necessarily compressive. The dimensionality reduction creates an exact identifiability boundary.
13.2 Rank-nullity theorem: the unavoidable information loss
This is not a numerical weakness of a particular implementation. It is a structural theorem. If B has full row rank, exactly five independent latent directions can affect the 5-D output and 123 independent directions remain invisible to that output. If rank(B) < 5, the invisible subspace is even larger.
rank(B) = 5  =>  dim ker(B) = 123.
13.3 Observable and nullspace decomposition
For a fixed linear bridge, let B^+ denote the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. Define the row-space projector and nullspace projector
P_obs = B^+ B,     P_null = I_128 - B^+ B.
Every latent state decomposes orthogonally as
z = P_obs z + P_null z.

Figure 13.2 - The kinetic output determines only the bridge-observable component. The nullspace component is erased by the map and cannot be reconstructed from y alone.
A reconstruction from y therefore requires a second model that chooses among the affine family B^+y + ker(B). The chosen prior must be reported separately from the information actually carried by y.
13.4 Fitting a linear bridge without hiding the model
Suppose N paired samples are available, with latent columns X in R^(128 x N) and kinetic columns Y in R^(5 x N). A ridge-regularized bridge solves
B_lambda = argmin_B ||Y - BX||_F^2 + lambda ||B||_F^2.
For lambda > 0, the closed-form primal solution is
B_lambda = Y X^T (X X^T + lambda I_128)^(-1).
This formula is a model-fitting result, not evidence of causal transport. Feature scaling, lambda, sample selection, missing-data treatment, and any low-rank restriction are part of the frozen bridge specification.
13.5 State-prediction defect and scale-normalized error
For paired holdout state (z,y), define the direct bridge residual
e_B(z,y) = y - Bz.
A dimensionless symmetric defect is useful for cross-dataset comparison:
rho_B(z,y) = ||y - Bz||_2 / (||y||_2 + ||Bz||_2 + epsilon).
The denominator prevents a change in units or overall scale from being mistaken for improved bridge quality. A threshold theta_B must be calibrated on training/calibration data and frozen before holdout evaluation; no universal numeric threshold is assumed.
13.6 Residual transport is a separate claim
A bridge may predict kinetic state reasonably while failing to preserve a residual, uncertainty, mirror symmetry, or other structure. Let R_128 be a typed latent residual operator, R_5 the corresponding kinetic residual operator, and G a declared translation between residual types. Define
tau_R(z) = || R_5(Bz) - G(R_128(z)) ||.
13.7 Uncertainty propagation and the cost of imputation
If z has covariance Sigma_z and B is linear and frozen, first-order uncertainty propagation is exact:
Sigma_y = B Sigma_z B^T.
For a nonlinear bridge y = B_theta(z), the local first-order approximation uses the Jacobian J_B(z):
Sigma_y approx J_B(z) Sigma_z J_B(z)^T.
Coordinates repaired by imputation must not inherit the same certainty as direct observations unless a calibrated imputation model justifies it. The observation mask from Part 12 therefore remains part of the bridge input or uncertainty model rather than being discarded after repair.
13.8 Tangent transport and model drift
Part 05 estimates one-sided kinetic tangents. If B is a constant linear map and z(t) is differentiable, then
y(t) = B z(t)  =>  y_dot(t) = B z_dot(t).
This identity fails in its simple form if the bridge itself changes with time. For B(t),
y_dot(t) = B(t) z_dot(t) + B_dot(t) z(t).
The extra drift term B_dot(t)z(t) is a direct confounder. A periodically retrained bridge can therefore manufacture apparent kinetic acceleration unless model-version changes are represented explicitly.
tau_v(t) = || v_5(t) - B v_128(t) ||_2
is the natural tangent-transport defect when both tangent estimates are independently available.
13.9 Duality compatibility across spaces
Part 10 defined signed-reversal duality operators. Let H_128 act in the latent space and H_5 in the kinetic space. A bridge preserves the declared duality when the following diagram commutes:
B H_128 = H_5 B.
The normalized commutator defect is
tau_H = || B H_128 - H_5 B ||_F / (||B||_F + epsilon).

Figure 13.3 - Mirror/duality transport is a commutation test. A small state-prediction error alone does not prove that the dual structure survives the bridge.
The same pattern can be used for any structure-preservation claim: define the operation in both spaces, declare the expected transport relation, and measure its defect on frozen holdout data.
13.10 Identifiability can be recovered only with added structure
Rank-nullity forbids unique inversion over all of R^128, but uniqueness can become possible on a restricted latent family. Let M subset R^128 be the admissible latent manifold. The bridge is injective on M if
z_1, z_2 in M and Bz_1 = Bz_2  =>  z_1 = z_2.
This is a property of the pair (B,M), not of B alone. Examples of additional structure include a manifold of intrinsic dimension at most five, a sparse support model with a proven recovery condition, or a dynamical model supplying enough independent observations over time.

The bridge can be extremely useful without being reversible. 15.2 Retrospective rolling-origin protocol
For each tested historical origin t, the forecasting loop supplies the model family only with values y_1,...,y_{t-1}. Four deliberately different model views are used where available: persistence, bounded local linear trend, ridge autoregression, and a seasonal mirror. The point forecast is the median of the available model predictions.
m_t = median(m_{t,1}, ..., m_{t,J})
D_t = max_j m_{t,j} - min_j m_{t,j}
The disagreement residual D_t is compared with the 65th percentile of preceding calibration-window disagreement values. The uncertainty interval half-width q_t is the finite-sample 90% quantile of preceding absolute forecast errors. A forecast is committed only if present disagreement does not exceed its historical limit.
COMMIT_t  iff  D_t <= Q_0.65({D_s : s < t in calibration window})
FalseCertainty_t = 1[ |y_t - m_t| > q_t ]

15.4 Aggregate validation result
Across all eight datasets, the gate retained 792 of 1,257 rolling forecasts. Always-commit interval coverage was 89.499%; conditional coverage among admitted forecasts was 91.919%. The false-certainty rate therefore declined from 10.501% to 8.081%, a 23.049% relative reduction.
Relative reduction = (0.1050119 - 0.0808081) / 0.1050119 = 0.2304867


Figure 15.3 - Aggregate reliability metrics. The gate improves conditional coverage while deliberately reducing decision frequency.
15.5 Selective risk separation
The aggregate improvement is easier to interpret by separating forecasts the gate admitted from those it rejected. The admitted set contains 64 false-certainty events among 792 forecasts; the rejected set contains 68 among 465.
Risk_admitted = 64/792 = 8.081%
Risk_rejected = 68/465 = 14.624%
Risk ratio = Risk_rejected / Risk_admitted = 1.810x
The gate rejected 36.99% of forecasts yet that rejected set contained 51.52% of all false-certainty events. Relative to random rejection at the same rate, false-certainty events were enriched in the rejected set by approximately 1.39x. These are descriptive retrospective quantities, not independent causal estimates.

Figure 15.4 - Rejected forecasts were about 1.81 times as likely to exceed their preceding historical error interval as admitted forecasts.
15.6 Dataset-level behavior and the reliability/accuracy split

The dataset table is important because uncertainty reliability and point-forecast accuracy are not the same objective. Unemployment produced the largest coverage gain (+7.95 percentage points) while committed point forecasts were worse than persistence. Treasury-bill rate shows the same qualitative split. CO2 is the lone dataset on which gated coverage declined (-1.54 percentage points), even though committed point skill remained positive.

Figure 15.5 - Coverage change by dataset. Seven of eight series improved; CO2 moved in the opposite direction.
15.7 Exploratory Disagreement Stress Ratio
The archived gate is binary. A useful post-hoc diagnostic is the dimensionless stress ratio between current model spread and the rolling disagreement limit:
Z_t = D_t / D_limit,t
Using the archived prediction table, define GREEN for Z <= 1, AMBER for 1 < Z <= 2, and RED for Z > 2. This tri-state partition was derived after the original campaign and therefore remains exploratory until frozen prospectively.

The RED zone contained only 3.90% of forecasts but 14.39% of all false-certainty events. Its false-certainty rate was 38.78%, approximately 3.69 times the unconditional rate. This suggests a possible future GRANT / QUALIFY / REFUSE governor, but it is not part of the original frozen protocol.

Figure 15.6 - Exploratory stress zones. The post-hoc RED region is strongly enriched for false-certainty events and requires fresh validation.
15.8 Temporal non-anticipation and the bitemporal boundary
Within the forecast loop, every prediction at origin t is generated from y[:t], and both the historical error interval and disagreement threshold are computed from earlier origins. This satisfies algorithmic rolling-origin non-anticipation for the tested prediction windows.

CO2 preprocessing deserves a precise note. The weekly series is resampled to monthly means and globally interpolated. Five monthly values are missing before interpolation: 1958-06, 1958-10, 1964-02, 1964-03, 1964-04. The earliest tested CO2 forecast origin is 1973-07, so the interpolation does not draw on observations after any tested forecast origin. It nevertheless prevents the dataset from being a pure archival-vintage reconstruction of those early months.
15.9 Dependence, uncertainty, and inferential discipline
Rolling forecast errors overlap in time and are generally serially dependent. The gate threshold is itself estimated from recent windows, and several datasets share macroeconomic provenance. Consequently, ordinary independent-and-identically-distributed p-values would overstate the evidentiary precision of these descriptive differences.

PERSISTENT REALITY
Part 16 - Blind Discovery and Falsification
Frozen Manifests | Blind Holdouts | Chronology-Safe Controls | Leakage Firewall | Negative Controls | Promotion Gates | Prospective Replication
16.1 Purpose: from retrospective evidence to prospective discipline
Part 15 established a reproducible retrospective result: a disagreement-based residual gate selectively abstained on harder historical forecasts and improved aggregate uncertainty coverage in the archived campaign. The next scientific question is not whether that computation can be described more strongly; it is whether a rule frozen before seeing new outcomes retains the effect on untouched data. Part 16 therefore defines the protocol that separates discovery from confirmation.
D = D_discovery ⊔ D_validation,   D_discovery ∩ D_validation = ∅
The symbol ⊔ denotes a deliberately disjoint partition. Discovery data may be used freely for model design, threshold selection, diagnostics, and hypothesis generation. Validation data may be used only under a precommitted analysis. If validation outcomes influence the method, those observations cease to be an untouched validation set for that method.

Figure 16.1 - Canonical discovery-to-promotion protocol. Adaptation after the freeze is allowed only by explicitly returning the affected result to discovery status.
16.2 Frozen manifest and experiment identity
A prospective test is identified by a frozen manifest M containing every decision that could materially change the reported outcome. The manifest is serialized canonically and committed by cryptographic hash before the validation outcomes are inspected.
h_M = SHA-256(canonical_json(M))


Figure 16.2 - The frozen manifest is the experiment identity; its hash commits the analysis before holdout outcomes are available.
16.3 Blinding and opaque identifiers
Where labels can reveal entity identity, region, era, source family, or outcome class, the analysis should operate on opaque identifiers. The re-identification map is sealed before the blind run and opened only after the frozen outputs are committed.
b_i = HMAC_k(canonical_id_i)
A keyed digest is preferred to short unhashed aliases because it resists accidental semantic leakage and collision-based aliasing. At least 128 bits of effective identifier strength should be retained when identifiers are used as blinds. The key and mapping are provenance objects, not analysis features.
16.4 Chronology-safe replay and the knowledge-time filtration
Historical replay requires more than sorting by event date. At analysis time t, an observation is admissible only if its knowledge/availability time was no later than t. This prevents later revisions, future publications, and post-event reconstructions from leaking into an ostensibly historical state.
F_t = σ(Y_i : t_available(i) ≤ t)
A_t is admissible only if A_t is F_t-measurable
The bitemporal record from Parts 02, 06, and 15 therefore remains mandatory: event time and availability time are separate fields. Retrospective rolling-origin replay using a final revised dataset is valuable, but it is not equivalent to a true historical information-time reconstruction.
16.5 Falsification battery
A strong result should survive controls that preserve irrelevant structure and fail controls that destroy the structure the claim says it needs. The control suite is claim-conditioned: no single perturbation is a universal falsifier.

Figure 16.3 - Example control-to-claim map. Controls are selected because they target specific assumptions, not because more controls automatically create more evidence.
16.6 Duplicate and narrative injection as epistemic negative controls
The provenance framework makes two unusually direct negative controls possible. First, duplicate injection adds exact or near-exact copies of existing records. Second, narrative injection adds summaries, paraphrases, AI-generated restatements, or symbolic reinterpretations that contain no new observation. A properly lineage-aware system should not award either operation new independent empirical support.
B = f(A), no new observation  ⇒  I(X; B | A) = 0
Support(A ∪ duplicates(A)) = Support(A)   after lineage collapse
Failure of either equality is a provenance bug: the system is manufacturing confidence from repetition or representation change.
16.7 Leakage firewall and adaptation policy

Figure 16.4 - Leakage firewall. Post-freeze adaptation is permitted only by reclassifying the affected analysis as discovery and obtaining a new untouched validation set.
The firewall is procedural rather than rhetorical. Every analysis run records the manifest hash, code hash, data partition hash, analyst-visible metadata class, and whether any holdout outcome was inspected. A changed hash is a new experiment identity. Repeated peeking without a predeclared sequential-testing rule is not a continuation of the same confirmatory test.
16.8 Statistical promotion without independence inflation
The validation protocol must match the dependence structure of the data. Historical forecast errors are serially dependent and may also share macroeconomic or measurement shocks across series. Ordinary iid p-values are therefore not a default promotion criterion. Depending on the design, suitable approaches can include block bootstrap intervals, cluster-aware resampling, predeclared permutation tests that preserve chronology, or hierarchical replication across independent source lineages.
If several candidate metrics or thresholds are tested, the multiplicity rule must be frozen. Family-wise error control, false-discovery-rate control, or a single predeclared primary endpoint are all legitimate choices when their assumptions match the design; selecting the favorable rule after seeing outcomes is not.
16.9 Promotion ladder

Figure 16.5 - Evidence promotion ladder. Each step requires a new constraint on researcher degrees of freedom and, at the upper levels, genuinely new data or lineage.
Universal, causal, mechanistic, or physical-law claims require additional domain-specific evidence beyond reaching E4 on a predictive statistic. The typed support vector from Part 09 remains controlling: strong predictive support cannot automatically fill mechanism or universality coordinates.
16.10 Canonical promotion gate
A candidate proposition P is promoted only if every gate required by its declared claim type passes. The gate is intentionally conjunctive: one excellent statistic cannot compensate for temporal leakage, provenance dependence, or failed negative controls.
PROMOTE(P) = G_freeze ∧ G_blind ∧ G_time ∧ G_provenance ∧ G_control ∧ G_stat ∧ G_claim
If any required G_j = 0, then PROMOTE(P) = 0 and the failure is retained.
16.11 Application to the Part 15 disagreement-stress ratio
The GREEN / AMBER / RED disagreement-stress zones derived in Part 15 were constructed after inspection of the archived campaign. Under the present protocol they are therefore Discovery Hypothesis DSR-01, not a confirmatory result. The exact historical enrichment remains a valid descriptive fact of the archived data; the threshold structure must be frozen before any new evaluation if it is to be promoted.
16.12 Canonical execution algorithm
1. Define claim P and typed requirement vector C(P).
2. Split discovery and validation data before final model selection.
3. Build bitemporal/provenance records and opaque IDs.
4. Freeze features, models, thresholds, controls, statistics, stopping rule, and exclusions.
5. Canonicalize manifest M; commit h_M and code/data hashes.
6. Execute validation without inspecting intermediate outcomes except as predeclared.
7. Run chronology, provenance, negative-control, and falsification batteries.
8. Compute frozen primary endpoint and dependence-aware uncertainty.
9. Apply all required promotion gates conjunctively.
10. Commit PROMOTE / QUALIFY / REFUSE plus failure diagnostics to the negative-precedent ledger.
11. Unblind only after outputs and hashes are sealed.
12. Any post-hoc refinement starts a new discovery cycle.

17.1 Scope and Dependencies
Part 17 formalizes what the framework does when evidence does not close. It unifies the feasible-set reconstruction of Part 06, lineage independence of Part 07, typed solvency of Part 09, frozen falsification of Part 16, and the retained-consequence principle from Part 01. The objective is not to eliminate disagreement; it is to prevent incompatible evidence from being averaged into false certainty.

17.2 Disagreement, Contradiction, and Conflict
Disagreement is a difference between reports, estimates, models, or constraints. Exact contradiction is stronger: the admissible sets have no common state. A soft conflict is weaker: exact feasibility may remain, but the jointly best reconciliation has large normalized residual.
Exact:  F = ⋂ᵢ Fᵢ = ∅
Soft:   J*(F) = minₓ Σᵢ wᵢ [δᵢ(x)/sᵢ]²


Figure 17.1 - Exact contradiction and soft residual conflict are different mathematical objects and require different governance actions.
17.3 Pairwise Consistency Is Not Joint Consistency
Counterexample in R²:
F₁={x≥0},   F₂={y≥0},   F₃={x+y≤−1}
Each pair is feasible: (1,1) satisfies F₁∩F₂, (0,−2) satisfies F₁∩F₃, and (−2,0) satisfies F₂∩F₃. But no point can satisfy x≥0 and y≥0 while also satisfying x+y≤−1. Hence F₁∩F₂∩F₃=∅.

Figure 17.2 - A concrete pairwise-consistent but jointly inconsistent constraint family.
17.4 Minimal Inconsistent Cores
When the full system is inconsistent, the useful object is not the entire corpus but a smallest locally incompatible subset.
C ⊆ {1,…,n} is a MIC iff  ⋂ᵢ∈C Fᵢ=∅  and  ∀j∈C: ⋂ᵢ∈C∖{j} Fᵢ≠∅
A MIC localizes incompatibility. It still does not identify which member is false. Several members may be individually accurate but jointly incompatible because they refer to different times, definitions, populations, units, or latent-state assumptions.
17.5 Provenance-Aware Contradiction
Exact and soft conflict analysis should run on independent provenance lineages, not raw document count. Copies, rephrasings, exports, mirrors, and AI summaries derived from one source are one evidentiary ancestry unless new independent observation enters the lineage.
F_lineage = ⋂_ℓ F_ℓ,   where each F_ℓ is formed after duplicate/derivative collapse

Figure 17.3 - Canonical contradiction workflow: collapse ancestry first, then localize and diagnose conflict.
17.6 Leave-Lineage-Out Conflict Relief
For soft conflict, define the globally minimized objective J*. Remove one lineage ℓ, recompute the optimum, and measure the reduction:
Δ_ℓ = J* − J*_(−ℓ)  ≥ 0
Large Δ_ℓ means that removing lineage ℓ substantially reduces the current incompatibility. It is a localization diagnostic, not a guilt score. A lineage can produce large relief because it is uniquely informative, differently calibrated, temporally misaligned, or genuinely erroneous.

17.7 Robust Claim Status Under Incomplete Reconstruction
A claim can sometimes be decided even when the latent state is not unique. Let P⊆Ω be the proposition region and F the surviving feasible state set.
SUPPORTED: F⊆P      REFUTED: F∩P=∅      UNRESOLVED: otherwise
17.8 Negative Precedent as Retained Consequence
A failed hypothesis is not discarded from memory. Its failure becomes a retained consequence that changes the future hypothesis space.
H_(n+1) = H_n ∖ F_n  ⊆ H_n
This theorem is intentionally narrow. A noisy or model-dependent failure should not automatically delete a hypothesis. Soft failures are retained with reduced support, increased cost, or explicit re-entry conditions.

Figure 17.4 - Hard negative precedent contracts the viable hypothesis set; soft conflict should alter support rather than force deletion.

18.2 Typed Transport Maps
Let domain A have state space Ω_A, operations O_A, residuals R_A, unit signatures U_A, chronology T_A, and provenance P_A. Let domain B have corresponding typed objects. A candidate transport is not one number; it is a bundle of maps:
F: Ω_A→Ω_B,   F_O: O_A→O_B,   G_R: R_A→R_B,   G_U: U_A→U_B,   G_T: T_A→T_B,   G_P: P_A→P_B

18.3 Residual-Commutation Defect
For a source-domain residual R_A and target residual R_B, define a residual translation G_R. The transport defect is
τ_F(x,y)=||R_B(Fx,Fy)−G_R(R_A(x,y))||

Figure 18.2 - Residual transport is a commutation problem. The target residual must agree with the transported source residual, not merely look similar.
18.4 Dimensional and Unit Compatibility
Dimensional analysis is a fast refusal gate. Represent the physical dimension of a quantity q by an exponent vector u(q) over a chosen base, for example [M,L,T,I,Θ,N,J]. A lawful unit transport requires an explicit map A_U such that
u_B(F(q)) = A_U u_A(q)
For same-physics unit changes, A_U typically preserves dimension and only numerical scale changes. For abstract dimensionless features, the mapping must explicitly state that the target object is also dimensionless. A numerically convenient equality between incompatible dimensions is not a transport law.
18.5 Provenance and Epistemic Novelty Under Transport
Cross-domain transformation does not manufacture independent evidence. If B=f(A) is deterministically constructed from source evidence A and no new observation enters, then the transformed object remains in the same evidentiary ancestry.
I(X; B | A)=0   for deterministic B=f(A) with no new observation
18.6 Structural Transport Is Not Causal Transport
Preserving a metric, residual, symmetry, or graph pattern does not prove that the same mechanism generates the pattern in both domains. Causal transport requires separately identified intervention or mechanism structure. The canonical claim should therefore distinguish:


Figure 18.3 - A cross-domain claim is admitted only through the gates actually required by its semantic scope.
18.7 Injectivity, Information Loss, and Reconstruction
Part 13 supplies a concrete case: a linear bridge B:R^128→R^5 has rank at most 5 and therefore nullity at least 123. It may be a useful predictive compression while remaining fundamentally noninvertible on the unrestricted 128-D space.
rank(B)≤5  ⇒  dim ker(B)≥123
18.8 Composition and Defect Accumulation
Cross-domain claims are often chained: A→B→C. Exact maps compose exactly. Approximate maps require a stability bound. Suppose the B→C residual translation G₂ is L-Lipschitz and the two stage defects satisfy ||e₁||≤ε₁ and ||e₂||≤ε₂. Then
τ_(F₂∘F₁) ≤ L ε₁ + ε₂

Figure 18.4 - Approximate transport can accumulate error. Controlled composition requires explicit stability bounds.
18.9 Finite Validation Does Not Prove Global Equivalence
This prevents a recurring promotion error: a handful of impressive correspondences cannot be called a universal law simply because the measured defect happens to be zero on the inspected examples.

19.3 AI and Adaptive-Agent Governance
The recursive computational corpus repeatedly returns to a common loop: observe, compare, classify, bound, test, repair, retain, and transform. In an agent system this becomes a governance shell around any planner, learned policy, or heuristic controller. The shell is useful even when the internal intelligence is replaced.

Figure 19.3 - Agent governance loop. Retention changes later admissible actions, so the governance state is history-bearing rather than a stateless classifier.
Canonical agent state

A proposed action a_t is evaluated before execution. The governor checks resource solvency, evidence support, policy constraints, uncertainty, and retained negative precedent. If a hard gate fails, the correct output is refusal or qualification rather than forced action.
a_t → {ADMIT, QUALIFY, REFUSE, REPAIR}
Useful implementations include:
tool-using agents that must distinguish observed data from imputed or generated content;
adaptive controllers that must roll back when residuals reopen;
multi-agent systems that must retain provenance and avoid counting correlated agents as independent evidence;
automated review systems that preserve refuted claims as negative precedent instead of rediscovering them.

19.4 Engineering Control and Resource Solvency
The most direct engineering translation of the governing invariant is resource admission. Let q be a requested resource vector and I_t the measured interior or remaining budget. In compatible units:
q ⪯ I_t
The comparison is componentwise across quantities such as compute, memory, electrical power, thermal headroom, duty cycle, bandwidth, structural load, or stored energy. The governor must refuse any commitment that exceeds a hard resource coordinate even if every other coordinate remains solvent.
A physically meaningful energy ledger should close across all measured ports:
R_E = E_in − E_out − E_loss − ΔE_stored
“Recovered energy” is admitted only within measurement uncertainty and cannot exceed the measured balance without a documented missing port or model correction.

19.8 Geometry, Interaction Networks, and Materials Research
Part 08 supplies an exact mathematical application layer for systems in which ordinary geometric separation and independently measured interaction geometry can be compared. The corrected Howard Comma is:
H_ij = d_ij − λ* D_I(i,j)
When the interaction kernel is positive semidefinite and independently constructed, D_I is a legitimate feature-space distance and H_ij is a signed discrepancy. This can be applied to contact networks, porous structures, transport graphs, lattice experiments, biological networks, or communication networks - but only after each domain defines its own measurable interaction features.
Vesica / overlap geometry
The exact 5/16 equal-sphere overlap ratio at center separation d=r is usable as geometry. The Kepler density is usable for non-overlapping equal-sphere packing. Their coexistence in a two-radius model is a valid construction. None of those facts alone proves a new material phase, a universal “still-point,” or a specific macroscopic mechanical property.
Suggested materials experiment
3-D print or machine parameterized lattices with independently varied core radius and interaction/strut radius;
measure stiffness, buckling, permeability, damping, thermal conduction, and mass fraction;
compute Howard residuals between physical distance and independently measured functional interaction distance;
freeze candidate geometric predictors, then test on held-out lattice families.


19.9 Frequency, Resonance, Biological, and Medical Boundaries
The corpus contains frequency, resonance, scar-tissue, tumor, and broader biological hypotheses. These are retained as hypotheses or design inspirations, not promoted into therapeutic claims. The canonical monograph explicitly refuses universal healing-frequency claims, and the same boundary governs this application section.
Permitted research framing
Use audio or vibration frequencies as controlled experimental inputs when an appropriate biological or materials experiment is ethically and technically designed.
Measure dose, coupling path, exposure, temperature, mechanical strain, acoustic pressure, and outcome variables rather than inferring internal effects from nominal Hz alone.
Treat pleasant binaural or auditory experiences as perceptual/audio phenomena unless a separate physiological endpoint is measured.
For disease treatment, require appropriate preclinical/clinical evidence and qualified medical oversight; do not substitute headphones or unvalidated resonance protocols for established care.

For a safety-critical application, uncertainty is itself a resource claim. If uncertainty exceeds the validated operating envelope, the system must degrade, abstain, revert to a safe baseline, or request human intervention. “Continue because the model is confident” is not an acceptable substitute for a validated safety case.

19.12 Domain Implementation Blueprint
Every future application chapter, prototype, or proposal should ship with the same compact package:
1. Domain statement - what physical, computational, historical, or biological system is being modeled.
2. Typed state vector - quantities, units, valid ranges, missingness semantics, and chronology.
3. Domain adapter - explicit maps from observations to state and from state to decisions.
4. Residual registry - each residual named by failure mode; no cancellation across unrelated types.
5. Support/claim vectors - what evidence supports existence, timing, magnitude, causality, mechanism, and universality.
6. Resource and safety interiors - hard operational limits, uncertainty margins, and safe fallback behavior.

Theorem 1.1 - Retained-Consequence Insufficiency.
Let a represented state X_n and admissible input U_n be fixed. Suppose there exist retained states m and m' such that F(X_n,m,U_n) != F(X_n,m',U_n). Then no single-valued transition rule f(X_n,U_n) can reproduce both evolutions. Consequently X_n alone is not a sufficient deterministic state representation for that transition problem.
Theorem 1.2 - Stochastic state insufficiency.
If there exist m and m' such that K(· | X_n,m,U_n) != K(· | X_n,m',U_n), then the conditional transition distribution cannot in general be represented by a kernel depending only on X_n and U_n without averaging over an additional distribution for the omitted memory state.
Proposition 1.3 - Markov completion.
If all information from earlier history that affects the next-step transition is captured in M_n, and the update of M_n itself depends only on the current augmented state and current input/event, then Z_n=(X_n,M_n) is Markov with respect to the declared model: the future conditional law depends on the past only through Z_n.

State is not necessarily a list of currently visible object properties. At its most general, it is a compression of history that preserves every distinction needed for the future questions the model is supposed to answer.

Definition 2.1 - Epistemic solvency.

This Part defines the four-space partition used throughout the remainder of Persistent Reality. The partition is an analytical framework: its value lies in preventing category errors and making transitions between reality, evidence, models, and future alternatives explicit and auditable.
Foundational rule.
A statement may be meaningful in more than one space, but its evidentiary status must be evaluated separately in each. Movement between spaces is performed by declared maps, not by rhetorical substitution.

Irreversibility of occurrence.
Within the historical model, once an event has occurred its occurrence status is not changed by later reinterpretation. What can change is the record, reconstruction, confidence, classification, or model of that event.
Theorem 3.1 - Record-existence boundary.
From the existence of a record r whose content asserts proposition P, one may infer that the record exists and that it contains or encodes P. One may not infer P itself without an additional reliability/observation premise connecting the record to the occurrence space.
Model-status rule.
Good fit establishes compatibility between a model and admitted observations under the declared loss function. It does not by itself establish uniqueness, causality, mechanism, or universality.
Theorem 3.2.
If two distinct models M_1 and M_2 produce the same predicted observations for every admitted test in D, then D alone cannot distinguish M_1 from M_2.

No de-distortion miracle.
A transformation can reorganize or denoise information that remains in the record. It cannot universally recover distinctions that the observation process erased.

This Part defines the present-centered coordinate convention used throughout the remainder of the paper. It establishes what the origin means, what it does not mean, how retained consequence survives coordinate translation, and why future possibility must remain distinct from realized history.
Foundational rule.
The present origin is a representation choice, not a physical reset. Translating X(tau) to zero preserves displacements, derivatives, constraints, retained memory, provenance, and all other state variables not explicitly transformed.
Definition 4.1 - Present-centered origin.
For a selected audit time tau, the present-centered origin is the translated coordinate frame S_tau(t)=X(t)-X(tau). By construction, S_tau(tau)=0. The equality is therefore exact and definitional.
Theorem 4.1 - Origin identity.
For every trajectory X(t) for which X(tau) is defined, S_tau(tau)=0.
Theorem 4.2 - Displacement invariance.
For any t1 and t2 in the same translated frame, S_tau(t2)-S_tau(t1)=X(t2)-X(t1). Hence all pairwise displacements are unchanged by the translation.
Corollary 4.2a - Derivative invariance.
If X is differentiable at t, then dS_tau/dt = dX/dt. If X is twice differentiable, the same holds for acceleration. Present-centering changes position coordinates but not local velocity or curvature information.
Theorem 4.3 - Retained-consequence preservation.
A coordinate translation applied only to X leaves M unchanged. Therefore a history-bearing system does not become memoryless merely because its observable coordinate is represented at zero.

Temporal precision.
"History has already happened" is an occurrence-space statement. It does not imply that the historical record or the model of history is complete, immutable, or perfectly known.
No-leakage rule.
Present-centering does not license future information. The coordinate origin and the knowledge-time cutoff are separate structures and must both be enforced.
Present asymmetry.
At a historical point, both incoming and later-realized outgoing tangents can eventually be estimated. At the live present, only the incoming side is historically available. The other side is possibility, not fact.

The present tangent provides direction; the feasible tangent cone provides admissible local interior. Future projection is admitted only to the extent that direction, curvature, evidence, and constraints jointly support it.

This Part derives the one-sided historical tangent estimator used throughout the remainder of the paper. Exact algebraic results are separated from estimation assumptions. Future projection is treated as a local conditional approximation, never as a realized future fact.
Core distinction.
The incoming tangent v^-(tau) describes the local direction inferred from information available before an audit time. The later outgoing tangent v^+(tau), when available retrospectively, describes realized post-audit motion. Their difference measures trajectory change; it does not by itself identify a cause.
Definition 5.1 - Anchored quadratic tangent model.
Given historical samples (t_i,y_i) with t_i<0, fit y_i approximately equal to v t_i + a t_i^2. The tangent estimate is v; the local quadratic coefficient is a; the instantaneous quadratic-model acceleration at the origin is 2a.
Implementation note.
The closed forms are useful for proofs and diagnostics. Numerically, a QR or SVD solve of the weighted design matrix is preferable when timestamps are poorly scaled or nearly degenerate.
Theorem 5.1 - Uniqueness of the anchored quadratic estimate.
Assume at least two samples have positive weight, nonzero timestamps, and distinct timestamp values. Then Delta>0 and the weighted anchored quadratic least-squares estimate (v_hat,a_hat) is unique.
Corollary 5.1a - Degeneracy diagnosis.
A singular or near-singular fit is not mysterious evidence of a special state. It indicates insufficient timestamp diversity, extreme numerical scaling, or effectively duplicated sampling locations.

This Part formalizes how latent reality is constrained by imperfect records. Exact set-theoretic results are separated from statistical modeling choices. A feasible set may narrow without collapsing to one point, and robust propositions may be identifiable even when the exact state is not.
Core boundary.
Reconstruction is permitted to narrow what remains possible. It is not permitted to manufacture a unique state merely because downstream software prefers a point estimate.
Definition 6.1 - Observation operator.
An observation operator O_s maps a latent state into the record space available to source s. It may discard dimensions, aggregate, quantize, censor, threshold, distort, or otherwise transform the underlying state.
Principle 6.1 - Set before point.
When the evidence supports a region of latent states, the canonical reconstruction object is that region. A point estimator may be added for a declared decision purpose, but it must not replace the underlying feasible set in the evidence ledger.
Theorem 6.1 - Non-injective observation implies possible non-identifiability.
If O_s is not injective on Omega, then there exist distinct latent states x_1 != x_2 with O_s(x_1)=O_s(x_2). Consequently an exact observation y_s=O_s(x_1) cannot, from that source alone, distinguish x_1 from x_2.
Corollary 6.1a - No universal perfect de-distortion.
A universal inverse that exactly recovers every latent state from a non-injective observation cannot exist without additional information, prior restrictions, or side constraints. Apparent recovery may still be possible on a restricted subset, but that restriction is part of the model and must be stated.
Theorem 6.2 - Monotone feasible-set narrowing.
For any additional constraint F_{m+1}, the updated feasible set satisfies F_{1:m+1}=F_{1:m} intersect F_{m+1} subseteq F_{1:m}.
Theorem 6.3 - Duplicate-constraint invariance.
For any feasible set F, F intersect F = F. Repeating an identical constraint cannot further narrow exact feasible-state geometry.
Operational rule.
Collapse exact or near-deterministic derivative records to their provenance lineage before computing independence-sensitive support. Preserve the derivative records for auditability, but do not let repetition inflate evidence interior.
Theorem 6.4 - Contradiction establishes incompatibility, not culprit identity.
If the joint feasible set is empty, the admitted constraints cannot all be true simultaneously under the declared observation and uncertainty models. This fact alone does not determine which source, calibration, timestamp, model, or assumption is wrong.
Consequence.
A contradiction engine must test the joint constraint system, or compute minimal inconsistent subsets, rather than infer consistency from pairwise agreement alone.
Typed interpretation.
Hard feasibility and soft optimization answer different questions. F != emptyset asks whether all hard constraints can hold simultaneously. x*=argmin J asks which compromise minimizes a declared penalty when exact joint satisfaction is unavailable or intentionally relaxed.

Theorem 6.5 - Robust claim identifiability.
A proposition P can be identified as true relative to the admitted constraint system even when the exact latent state is non-unique, provided F subseteq P. Likewise P is robustly refuted when F intersect P is empty.

THEOREM 16.1 - HOLDOUT CONTAMINATION BOUNDARY
If any parameter, feature, threshold, exclusion, stopping rule, or reported metric is modified using the outcomes of a validation set, then that set no longer provides an untouched confirmatory test of the modified procedure. The observations remain scientifically useful, but only as discovery data for the revised procedure. A new untouched set is required for confirmation.
THEOREM 16.2 - BLIND RELABELING INVARIANCE
Let π be a bijection on entity labels. If an analysis A uses only measured values, declared structure, and provenance relations invariant under π, then A(πD) must equal πA(D) up to the corresponding output relabeling. A material change under a semantics-free relabeling is evidence that label information or an equivalent proxy leaked into the computation.

Theorem 17.1 - Pairwise consistency is insufficient
There exist finite families of constraints for which every pair has nonempty intersection while the full intersection is empty. Therefore pairwise agreement checks cannot certify global consistency.
Theorem 17.2 - Existence in finite inconsistent systems
If a finite family of feasible-set constraints has empty total intersection, then at least one minimal inconsistent core exists. Proof: among all inconsistent subsets choose one of minimum cardinality; deleting any member must restore consistency, otherwise the chosen subset was not minimal.
Provenance rule
Ten contradictory copies of one underlying record are not ten independent contradictions. Likewise, ten agreeing copies do not supply ten independent confirmations.

Many derivative copies | One lineage is repeatedly represented. | Independent replication exists.
Theorem 17.3 - Robust claim identifiability
If every feasible latent state satisfies P, the claim is robustly supported despite state non-uniqueness. If no feasible state satisfies P, it is robustly refuted. Otherwise the evidence does not identify the claim and the correct status is unresolved.
Theorem 17.4 - Monotone contraction under hard falsification
If F_n contains only hypotheses rejected by a valid frozen falsifier, then H_(n+1)⊆H_n. The viable search space cannot grow merely by retaining the falsification.

Final verification rule
No statement in the rebuilt framework may inherit a stronger status from a neighboring claim. DERIVED | Exact numerical/algebraic consequence of a declared model or reproduced dataset. | Does not exceed the model/data from which it was derived.
REPRODUCED | A prior computation was independently rerun and matched the archived artifact. | Reproduction verifies computation, not external truth.
EMPIRICALLY SUPPORTED | Observed data support the bounded claim under the stated design. | Not universal; strength depends on design, chronology and independence.
CONDITIONAL | Valid definition, policy, protocol, or engineering statement when declared conditions hold. | Requires those conditions and may still need empirical validation.
OPEN | Not established or refuted under the current evidence. | Requires a specified new proof/test rather than rhetorical repetition.
REFUTED | The previously asserted formulation is contradicted by proof, counterexample, type error, dimensional error, or failed validation. | Retained as negative precedent; may return only as a materially revised claim.
No status by adjacency
If P is proved and Q merely resembles P, Q remains open until a valid map, proof, or experiment supports Q. This is the final operational form of the cross-domain and narrative firewalls.

1.1 No automatic promotion
The classes form a governance hierarchy, not a simple numeric ladder. For example, a C2 mathematical
theorem about a simulation may be exact while saying nothing about physical reality. A C5 empirical
result can support a narrow historical claim without establishing a C6 cross-domain mechanism.

evidence.

1.2 Claim vectors instead of one truth score
The master architecture separates support dimensions because evidence can be strong for one aspect of
a proposition and weak for another. For proposition P define a support vector

S(P) = [ S_E, S_T, S_Q, S_C, S_M, S_U ]^T
corresponding respectively to support for existence, timing, quantity or magnitude, causality,
mechanism, and universality. Let C(P) denote the support requirements of the proposed wording.

ADMIT(P) iff C(P) <= S(P) componentwise
Thus a record may strongly support that an event existed while weakly supporting its precise timing,
cause, mechanism, or universal significance.

Status may rise, fall, or split as new proofs, measurements, failures, source revisions, or

2. Core Distinctions That Must Never Collapse
2.1 Occurrence, record, model, and possibility
Occurrence != Record != Model != Possibility
Occurrence space contains what actually happened. Record space contains surviving traces. Model space
contains organized reconstructions, simulations, or explanations. Possibility space contains alternatives
not yet actualized, including counterfactuals and design hypotheses. A document may be real as an
artifact while fictional in depicted content; a simulation may be exact relative to its code while
empirically false about the world.

2.2 Reality, observation, and interpretation
Reality != Observation != Interpretation
All observations are mediated by access, instruments, perception, preservation, coding, language, or
reconstruction. The framework therefore reconstructs a feasible set of compatible states before forcing a
unique story.

R(Y) = F_Y subset of Omega

have been retained.

substituted for one another simply because all are dimensionless.

3. Provenance, Independence, and Evidence Novelty
3.1 Provenance record
Each evidence object should carry, at minimum: source identity, author or origin, event time where
relevant, acquisition time, publication/preservation time, knowledge/admissibility time, lineage
identifier, transformation history, evidence class, uncertainty, and integrity hash. Provenance is a graph
because one record may depend on multiple earlier records.

3.2 Repetition is not independence
The Drive corpus contains many exported, reformatted, mirrored, summarized, or copied versions of the
same underlying material. These are valuable for development history and integrity checks but cannot
automatically multiply independent empirical support.

Theorem 3.2.1 - Deterministic derivation does not create independent empirical novelty
Statement. If record B is a deterministic transformation of record A and introduces no new
independent observation of latent reality X, then B does not add empirical information about X
conditional on A.

B = f(A) and no new observation => I(X; B | A) = 0.
Proof / justification. This is the conditional form of the information data-processing principle:
after A is known, a deterministic recoding of A cannot reveal a new external observation that was
absent from A.
Plain English. A PDF export, summary, mirror rendering, or AI rewrite can reorganize evidence
but cannot manufacture a second observation of the world.
Status: Exact under the stated deterministic/no-new-observation condition.

3.3 Integrity is not truth
Cryptographic hashes can establish that bytes remained unchanged relative to a committed artifact.
They do not establish that the contents are accurate, causal, physically realized, or complete.

3.4 Independence must be earned
Distinct authors, languages, websites, models, or filenames do not prove evidentiary independence.
Independence is supported by traceable separation of source ancestry, acquisition process,
measurement channel, or causal information pathway.

3.5 Source classes are channels, not universal truth weights
Physical measurements, transactions, structured records, testimony, narrative, myth, fiction, and
simulation answer different questions. Their contribution should be conditioned on the claim dimension
being tested rather than assigned one permanent global truth weight.

4.1 Residual honesty
A residual is meaningful only when the compared descriptions were specified independently of the
residual that will later be interpreted. Reverse-engineering a representation so that the residual is small

The master paper uses typed residual components rather than one scalar that allows incompatible

A strong numerical fit cannot compensate for future-information leakage; low contradiction cannot

For source-compatible feasible sets F_i, exact contradiction occurs when their joint intersection is empty:

evidentiary support decreases. The paper therefore records both fit and coverage/missingness.

Every empirical quantity should identify its units, calibration basis, uncertainty or error bound, and

5. Time, Causality, and the Present Origin
5.1 Four times
A historical record may carry event time, acquisition time, preservation/publication time, and
knowledge/admissibility time. Forward replay may use a record only after its admissibility time. A later
record can improve retrospective reconstruction without being back-dated into an earlier prospective
analysis.

5.2 Current reality as a coordinate origin
The master paper uses a present-centered coordinate convention for trajectory analysis. If X(t) is an
absolute state and t_now is the current analysis time, define

S(t) = X(t) - X(t_now)
S(0) = 0
This is a coordinate translation, not a claim that physical reality has zero magnitude or zero energy. It
allows the realized past to approach a common live origin while the future remains a constrained
possibility field.

5.3 Historical tangents versus future realization
Historical tangents are retrospectively testable because later realized states are already known. The
present tangent is prospective: it estimates the local direction entering the origin, but its outgoing
deflection has not yet occurred. Future projections must therefore be described as possibility, forecast,
or model output rather than established reality.

5.4 Temporal precedence is not causal identification
A variable preceding another may be necessary for ordinary forward-time causation but is not sufficient
to establish it. Causal promotion requires stronger assumptions, interventions, mechanisms, or
otherwise justified identification strategies.

1. Process-First Foundation
Part identifier: PR-01
Document class: Foundational mathematics and systems model
Purpose: Define a general state-transition architecture for systems whose future reachability can depend
on retained consequences of prior interactions, while preserving the special case in which ordinary
object-first or memoryless state descriptions are sufficient.

1.1 Scope and claim boundary
Object-first description is indispensable in science and engineering. A point mass can be modeled by
state variables such as position and momentum; a digital controller can be modeled by a finite state; an
inventory can be represented by current quantities. The present framework does not reject those
descriptions. It asks a narrower question: is the chosen state representation sufficient to determine the
transition law relevant to the problem?
If two systems occupy the same represented state but can evolve differently under the same admissible
input because of omitted fatigue, hysteresis, stored internal state, learning, damage, memory, reputation,
prior loading, or another retained consequence, then the represented state is incomplete for that
transition problem. The appropriate repair is state augmentation, not metaphysical reinterpretation.
Canonical claim.
A state description is sufficient only relative to a declared transition problem. Retained consequence
matters exactly when omitted history changes the conditional law of future transitions.

1.7 The Retained-Consequence Insufficiency Theorem
Theorem 1.1 - Retained-Consequence Insufficiency.
Let a represented state X_n and admissible input U_n be fixed. Suppose there exist retained states m
and m' such that F(X_n,m,U_n) != F(X_n,m',U_n). Then no single-valued transition rule f(X_n,U_n) can

reproduce both evolutions. Consequently X_n alone is not a sufficient deterministic state
representation for that transition problem.
Proof.
Assume for contradiction that a single-valued rule f(X_n,U_n) reproduces the system while omitting M_n.
For the same X_n and U_n it must return one value f(X_n,U_n). But by hypothesis the physically or
logically admissible augmented states (X_n,m) and (X_n,m') produce two different next states under F.
One value cannot equal two unequal values. Therefore no such f can reproduce both transitions, and
X_n alone is insufficient. QED.
Plain English.
If two systems look identical according to the variables you recorded, receive the same input, and
nevertheless can respond differently because their histories left different internal consequences, then
the recorded variables do not contain enough state information to predict both responses.

1.8 Stochastic extension
Theorem 1.2 - Stochastic state insufficiency.
If there exist m and m' such that K(· | X_n,m,U_n) != K(· | X_n,m',U_n), then the conditional transition
distribution cannot in general be represented by a kernel depending only on X_n and U_n without
averaging over an additional distribution for the omitted memory state.
The stochastic result clarifies an important distinction. A reduced model may still predict average
behavior after marginalizing over hidden history, but its uncertainty then includes unresolved variation
from the omitted retained state. Good average prediction does not prove that the reduced representation
is mechanistically complete.

1.9 Markov completion by state augmentation
Proposition 1.3 - Markov completion.
If all information from earlier history that affects the next-step transition is captured in M_n, and the
update of M_n itself depends only on the current augmented state and current input/event, then
Z_n=(X_n,M_n) is Markov with respect to the declared model: the future conditional law depends on
the past only through Z_n.

Pr(Z_{n+1} | Z_0,...,Z_n,U_n) = Pr(Z_{n+1} | Z_n,U_n).
This is a modeling statement, not a guarantee that a proposed memory variable is complete. Empirical
validation is still required to determine whether an implemented M_n captures the relevant retained
consequences.

2.5 Theorem 2.1 - Single-source non-identifiability
Theorem 2.1 - Non-injective observations do not uniquely identify latent reality.
If O_i is not injective on the admissible latent state space, then there exist distinct x and x' with
O_i(x)=O_i(x'). Therefore the observation alone cannot uniquely distinguish those latent states.
Proof.
Non-injectivity means by definition that at least two distinct admissible latent states share the same
image under O_i. An analysis receiving only that image cannot determine which preimage occurred
without additional information. QED.
Plain English.
If two different realities can leave the same record, the record by itself cannot tell you which reality
occurred.

2.6 Theorem 2.2 - Monotone narrowing under added constraints
Theorem 2.2 - Added admitted constraints cannot enlarge the feasible set.
Let F^(m)=intersection from i=1 to m of F_i. Then F^(m+1)=F^(m) intersect F_(m+1) is a subset of
F^(m).
Proof. Every element of F^(m+1) must satisfy all first m constraints plus one additional constraint, so it
necessarily belongs to F^(m). QED.
This theorem concerns modeled compatibility, not truth generation. Adding a duplicate or dependent
constraint can fail to add new information, while adding an incorrect constraint can shrink the feasible
set around the wrong region. Provenance and quality therefore remain part of admissibility.

2.11 Vector-valued support
A single support score obscures the fact that evidence can strongly support one kind of statement and
weakly support another. For proposition P define

S(P) = [S_E, S_T, S_Q, S_C, S_M, S_U]^T,
where the coordinates correspond to support for existence, timing, quantity/magnitude, causality,
mechanism, and universality. Coordinates are normalized support variables only after their
construction is specified. Unless empirically calibrated, they must not be read as probabilities.

2.12 Claim requirements
The wording of a claim determines what support it requires. Represent that demand as

C(P) = [C_E, C_T, C_Q, C_C, C_M, C_U]^T.
For example, “an event occurred” primarily loads the existence coordinate; “event A caused event B
through mechanism M in all systems of this class” places substantial requirements on existence, timing,
causality, mechanism, and universality. The evidence does not become stronger merely because the
sentence becomes more ambitious.

2.13 Componentwise claim solvency
Definition 2.1 - Epistemic solvency.
A claim P is support-solvent when its requirement vector does not exceed the supported interior in
any required coordinate: C(P) <= S(P) componentwise.

ADMIT(P) iff C_j(P) <= S_j(P) for every required dimension j, subject to hard provenance, temporal, type,
and policy gates.
This is a partial order rather than a compensating average. Excess support for existence cannot pay a
deficit in causality; excellent fit cannot compensate for future-information leakage; and repeated copies
cannot compensate for missing independent provenance.

3. The Four Spaces
Part identifier: PR-03
Document class: Foundational ontological-epistemic partition
Purpose: Define occurrence, record, model, and possibility as distinct semantic spaces; specify

3.1 Why the partition is necessary
The dual-ledger architecture of Part 02 separates reality from knowledge. The four-space partition
refines that distinction. It prevents a surviving record from being treated as identical to an occurrence, a
fitted model from being treated as the latent process itself, or an imagined/reachable possibility from

semantic boundary without sufficient support for the stronger status.

Occurrence != Record != Model != Possibility.

A statement may be meaningful in more than one space, but its evidentiary status must be evaluated
separately in each. Movement between spaces is performed by declared maps, not by rhetorical

3.5 Record existence is not referent existence
Theorem 3.1 - Record-existence boundary.
From the existence of a record r whose content asserts proposition P, one may infer that the record
exists and that it contains or encodes P. One may not infer P itself without an additional
reliability/observation premise connecting the record to the occurrence space.
Proof.
Construct a counterexample in which two worlds contain the same record r but differ on whether P
occurred. Because the premise "r exists and asserts P" is true in both worlds while P is false in one, the
entailment from record existence to P is invalid without additional premises. QED.
Plain English.
A story, image, log, memory, simulation, or document is evidence that the item exists. Whether it is also
evidence that the depicted external event occurred depends on how the item was produced and
preserved.

3.6 Model space
Model space contains deliberate representations of occurrence or record structure. Models can be
descriptive, predictive, causal, mechanistic, statistical, geometric, symbolic, or computational. Their
validity is always conditional on purpose, assumptions, data, residuals, and falsifiers.

m = M(D, A, theta),
where D is the admitted evidence set, A is the assumption set, and theta denotes fitted or declared
parameters. Multiple distinct models may fit the same records, especially when the observation map is
non-injective or the dataset is limited.
Model-status rule.
Good fit establishes compatibility between a model and admitted observations under the declared loss
function. It does not by itself establish uniqueness, causality, mechanism, or universality.

Theorem 3.2.
If two distinct models M_1 and M_2 produce the same predicted observations for every admitted test

Proof. Any decision procedure restricted to the predicted observations on D receives identical outputs
from both models. Therefore no distinction can be made without adding a new test, assumption, or
observation outside that equivalence class. QED.
This result motivates adversarial tests, holdout validation, cross-domain transport defects, and negative
precedent later in the paper.

3.10 The past can be fixed while the record changes
The four-space partition resolves an apparent paradox. Historical occurrence is treated as fixed after
realization, yet historical knowledge can improve or deteriorate. New archives may be discovered;

5.20 Canonical summary

6.1 Latent reality and source-specific observation

Definition 6.1 - Observation operator.

6.3 Non-identifiability theorem
Theorem 6.1 - Non-injective observation implies possible non-identifiability.
If O_s is not injective on Omega, then there exist distinct latent states x_1 != x_2 with
O_s(x_1)=O_s(x_2). Consequently an exact observation y_s=O_s(x_1) cannot, from that source alone,
distinguish x_1 from x_2.
Proof. Non-injectivity means by definition that two distinct inputs share the same output. Both inputs
therefore belong to O_s^{-1}({y_s}). Unless additional constraints exclude one of them, the source-level
inverse image contains more than one state. Hence unique reconstruction is not established.
Corollary 6.1a - No universal perfect de-distortion.
A universal inverse that exactly recovers every latent state from a non-injective observation cannot
exist without additional information, prior restrictions, or side constraints. Apparent recovery may
still be possible on a restricted subset, but that restriction is part of the model and must be stated.

F_{1:m} := intersection_{s=1}^m F_s.
Each independently meaningful constraint can preserve, narrow, or eliminate the currently feasible

THEOREM 7.1 | Exact duplicate invariance theorem
If B = f(A) is a deterministic representation change and B adds no new independent observation or calibration
information, then conditioning on both A and B cannot add information about latent state X beyond conditioning

F_A intersect F_A = F_A.

7.5 Structural independence
Structural independence is stricter than file distinctness. Let A_obs(v) be the relevant upstream
observation set. A sufficient structural condition for two evidence items to be independent at the
provenance layer is disjoint relevant observation ancestry:

For exploratory summarization, a symmetric redundancy matrix R may encode pairwise dependence or

7.7 Lineage-collapsed support
Support aggregation is claim-conditioned. A safe default is to collapse exact or near-exact descendants
within a lineage before combining across genuinely distinct lineages. If s_i(P) is a calibrated support
contribution for claim P, one conservative lineage representative is:

s_L(P) = max_{i in lineage L} s_i(P).
The maximum prevents repeated descendants from multiplying support. How support is then combined
across independent lineages depends on the calibrated evidence model; no universal noisy-OR, sum,
product, or Bayesian rule is assumed without its corresponding assumptions.

The generated RTL updates a primary accumulator by p_g and a complementary accumulator by c_g,

THEOREM 11.6 | 20-bit storage, 21-bit intermediate

emits expressions of the form (w_primary + step_inc) % DEN. Under fixed-width HDL expression sizing,
failing to widen the addition can discard the carry before the modulus is applied. The intended integer

wire [20:0] c_sum = {1'b0,w_complement} + {1'b0,comp_inc};
wire [20:0] r_sum = {1'b0,w_primary} + {1'b0,w_complement};
wire [19:0] p_next = (p_sum >= DEN_W) ? (p_sum - DEN_W) : p_sum[19:0];
wire [19:0] c_next = (c_sum >= DEN_W) ? (c_sum - DEN_W) : c_sum[19:0];

THEOREM 11.7 | Finite-state exactness boundary
A deterministic hardware generator with a finite internal state and no nonperiodic external input
must eventually repeat a state and therefore become periodic. Since the alpha mechanical word is
aperiodic, no fixed finite-state machine can emit that infinite word exactly for unbounded time.
Exactness must therefore be horizon-bounded, externally supplied, or supported by unbounded state.
For a frozen finite validation horizon, an exact gate sequence may be stored directly, or generated from
sufficiently precise integer/fixed-point machinery whose equivalence is proved over that horizon. The
test requirement is bit-exact agreement with the mathematical definition, not merely a similar long-run
frequency.

13.2 Rank-nullity theorem: the unavoidable information loss
EXACT

Theorem 13.1 - Linear bridge nullspace bound
For every linear map B: R^128 -> R^5, rank(B) <= 5 and therefore dim ker(B) = 128 rank(B) >= 123.
Proof. By rank-nullity, dim ker(B) + rank(B) = 128. Because the codomain has
dimension 5, rank(B) cannot exceed 5. Hence dim ker(B) is at least 123.

This is not a numerical weakness of a particular implementation. It is a structural theorem. If B has full
row rank, exactly five independent latent directions can affect the 5-D output and 123 independent
directions remain invisible to that output. If rank(B) < 5, the invisible subspace is even larger.

A 5-number kinetic state cannot uniquely encode 128 arbitrary independent latent degrees of

13.17 Plain-language synthesis
The bridge can be extremely useful without being reversible. It may compress the parts of a 128-D latent

everything; it is whether it preserves the specific state, residual, tangent, symmetry, uncertainty, and
claim dimensions required for the declared task on data that were not used to construct the bridge.
This makes latent-to-kinetic transport a controlled act of model reduction rather than a semantic
shortcut. Compression is admitted; hidden reconstruction is refused.

15.2 Retrospective rolling-origin protocol
For each tested historical origin t, the forecasting loop supplies the model family only with values
y_1,...,y_{t-1}. Four deliberately different model views are used where available: persistence, bounded
local linear trend, ridge autoregression, and a seasonal mirror. The point forecast is the median of the
available model predictions.

D_t = max_j m_{t,j} - min_j m_{t,j}
The disagreement residual D_t is compared with the 65th percentile of preceding calibration-window
disagreement values. The uncertainty interval half-width q_t is the finite-sample 90% quantile of
preceding absolute forecast errors. A forecast is committed only if present disagreement does not exceed
its historical limit.

COMMIT_t iff D_t <= Q_0.65({D_s : s < t in calibration window})
FalseCertainty_t = 1[ |y_t - m_t| > q_t ]

15.8 Temporal non-anticipation and the bitemporal boundary
Within the forecast loop, every prediction at origin t is generated from y[:t], and both the historical error
interval and disagreement threshold are computed from earlier origins. This satisfies algorithmic
rolling-origin non-anticipation for the tested prediction windows.
IMPORTANT LIMITATION
The campaign is not a strict historical knowledge-time replay. The statsmodels datasets are
final/revised representations rather than reconstructed real-time vintages. Therefore the test
establishes retrospective pseudo-out-of-sample behavior on the archived series, not what an analyst
literally knew on each historical date.

CO2 preprocessing deserves a precise note. The weekly series is resampled to monthly means and
globally interpolated. Five monthly values are missing before interpolation: 1958-06, 1958-10, 1964-02,
1964-03, 1964-04. The earliest tested CO2 forecast origin is 1973-07, so the interpolation does not draw on
observations after any tested forecast origin. It nevertheless prevents the dataset from being a pure
archival-vintage reconstruction of those early months.

15.9 Dependence, uncertainty, and inferential discipline
Rolling forecast errors overlap in time and are generally serially dependent. The gate threshold is itself
estimated from recent windows, and several datasets share macroeconomic provenance. Consequently,
ordinary independent-and-identically-distributed p-values would overstate the evidentiary precision of
these descriptive differences.

16.1 Purpose: from retrospective evidence to prospective discipline
Part 15 established a reproducible retrospective result: a disagreement-based residual gate selectively
abstained on harder historical forecasts and improved aggregate uncertainty coverage in the archived
campaign. The next scientific question is not whether that computation can be described more strongly;

design, threshold selection, diagnostics, and hypothesis generation. Validation data may be used only
under a precommitted analysis. If validation outcomes influence the method, those observations cease to
be an untouched validation set for that method.

THEOREM 16.1 - HOLDOUT CONTAMINATION BOUNDARY
If any parameter, feature, threshold, exclusion, stopping rule, or reported metric is modified using the
outcomes of a validation set, then that set no longer provides an untouched confirmatory test of the
modified procedure. The observations remain scientifically useful, but only as discovery data for the
revised procedure. A new untouched set is required for confirmation.

A keyed digest is preferred to short unhashed aliases because it resists accidental semantic leakage and

THEOREM 16.2 - BLIND RELABELING INVARIANCE
Let π be a bijection on entity labels. If an analysis A uses only measured values, declared structure,
and provenance relations invariant under π, then A(πD) must equal πA(D) up to the corresponding
output relabeling. A material change under a semantics-free relabeling is evidence that label
information or an equivalent proxy leaked into the computation.

16.4 Chronology-safe replay and the knowledge-time filtration
Historical replay requires more than sorting by event date. At analysis time t, an observation is
admissible only if its knowledge/availability time was no later than t. This prevents later revisions,
future publications, and post-event reconstructions from leaking into an ostensibly historical state.

F_t = σ(Y_i : t_available(i) ≤ t)
A_t is admissible only if A_t is F_t-measurable
The bitemporal record from Parts 02, 06, and 15 therefore remains mandatory: event time and
availability time are separate fields. Retrospective rolling-origin replay using a final revised dataset is
valuable, but it is not equivalent to a true historical information-time reconstruction.

16.6 Duplicate and narrative injection as epistemic negative controls
The provenance framework makes two unusually direct negative controls possible. First, duplicate
injection adds exact or near-exact copies of existing records. Second, narrative injection adds
summaries, paraphrases, AI-generated restatements, or symbolic reinterpretations that contain no new
observation. A properly lineage-aware system should not award either operation new independent
empirical support.

B = f(A), no new observation ⇒ I(X; B | A) = 0
Support(A ∪ duplicates(A)) = Support(A) after lineage collapse
Failure of either equality is a provenance bug: the system is manufacturing confidence from repetition
or representation change.

The firewall is procedural rather than rhetorical. Every analysis run records the manifest hash, code
hash, data partition hash, analyst-visible metadata class, and whether any holdout outcome was
inspected. A changed hash is a new experiment identity. Repeated peeking without a predeclared
sequential-testing rule is not a continuation of the same confirmatory test.

NO-PEEKING RULE
The holdout may be evaluated once under the frozen primary analysis, or repeatedly only under a
predeclared sequential design with its own error-control rule. Exploratory inspection is allowed, but
it spends the holdout: subsequent claims from that set are discovery claims.

16.8 Statistical promotion without independence inflation
The validation protocol must match the dependence structure of the data. Historical forecast errors are
serially dependent and may also share macroeconomic or measurement shocks across series. Ordinary
iid p-values are therefore not a default promotion criterion. Depending on the design, suitable
approaches can include block bootstrap intervals, cluster-aware resampling, predeclared permutation
tests that preserve chronology, or hierarchical replication across independent source lineages.
If several candidate metrics or thresholds are tested, the multiplicity rule must be frozen. Family-wise
error control, false-discovery-rate control, or a single predeclared primary endpoint are all legitimate
choices when their assumptions match the design; selecting the favorable rule after seeing outcomes is
not.

EVIDENCE RULE
More analyses do not create more independent evidence when they reuse the same outcomes.
Promotion strength should increase primarily through untouched data, independent lineages, and
successful falsification controls.
